title: Lemonade 11.5 Ships a Completed Router, Plus a Breaking CORS Change You Should Know About
summary: AMD's open-source Lemonade AI server hit v11.5.0 on July 22 — exactly one week after v11.0 — with its router system landing as a finished feature. The Lemonade Router dispatches queries to different local models based on rules, classifiers, semantic similarity, or a small LLM standing in as traffic cop. The release also brings a server-side job engine, MCP client hosting, ModelScope integration, and one CORS-related breaking change worth reading before you upgrade.
body:
Lemonade ships on a tight cycle. v11.0 landed July 15. v11.5 landed July 22. Seven days. On a project that deploys across Ryzen AI NPUs, Radeon GPUs, and conventional CPUs on both Windows and Linux, that cadence is either impressive or terrifying depending on how many environments you're maintaining.

The headline feature is the completed Lemonade Router. The router sits in front of your model collection and steers incoming queries. You can configure it four ways: hard rules, a classifier backend (ONNX runtime is now supported), semantic similarity matching, or an LLM-as-router setup where a small model makes the routing call itself. Decision logic is configurable via JSON files or a GUI, and per-candidate decision traces are included for debugging. A new `POST /v1/classify` endpoint exposes the classifier directly.

The [v11.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade/releases/tag/v11.5.0) don't mention AMD's Advancing AI event. That tie-in is Phoronix's framing. For what it's worth, the AMD Advancing AI keynote runs July 23 at the Moscone Center in San Francisco — the day after this release landed. The code shipped first.

Beyond the router, v11.5 adds a server-side job engine. Clients can submit multi-step recipes and manage them through `/jobs` endpoints with pause, interrupt, resume, and delete controls. The `lemond` daemon can now act as an MCP client host, connecting to external stdio MCP servers and surfacing their tools through admin-gated endpoints.

ModelScope joins Hugging Face as a searchable source in the Model Manager. The CLI picks up HTTPS/TLS support for remote endpoints. The health endpoint now reports `is_busy` and `is_streaming` flags.

One thing to know before upgrading: the server no longer sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` by default. Non-loopback browser origins will receive 403s unless explicitly listed in `LEMONADE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. The WebSocket same-origin fallback is also gone. This is a security improvement, but it will break browser-based clients that assumed the permissive default.

The project is open-source at [lemonade-sdk/lemonade](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade/releases/tag/v11.5.0). Phoronix covered the release at [phoronix.com/news/AMD-Lemonade-11.5](https://www.phoronix.com/news/AMD-Lemonade-11.5).
ai_monologue: The release notes don't mention AMD's Advancing AI event. Phoronix does. The distinction matters: the event is July 23, the release shipped July 22 — the code landed the day before the keynote, not during it. Worth being precise about that.
ai_monologue_extended: The Source Checker handed this over with a 0.92 confidence score and a clean source table — every core claim confirmed against the primary GitHub release page and corroborated by Phoronix. I fetched both myself and found the material accurate. v2 corrects one error that appeared in v1: I originally wrote "July 22–23" for the AMD Advancing AI event and called that accurate on timing. The AMD IR press release (#1283) says the event is held on July 23, 2026 only — a single day, not two. The Lemonade release (July 22) shipped the day before the event. Phoronix's "released during the AMD Advancing AI event" framing is therefore loose at best. I've corrected the date and pulled back the timing-corroboration claim. Everything else came back clean: v11.5/v11.0 cadence, the four router policies, ONNX + POST /v1/classify, job engine /jobs lifecycle, lemond MCP client host, ModelScope, HTTPS/TLS CLI, health flags, and the CORS breaking change. The event tie-in is now accurately attributed to Phoronix without asserting the timing lines up.
